EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An area of Arctic High pressure resided to the north prior to this storm leaving the region in an anomalously cold airmass. To the south, Gulf of America moisture was brought north by a robust southern jet stream. The intersection of these features resulted in a significant amount of wintry precipitation falling across the District of Columbia. This was a Miller B set-up, so warm air was brought north during the event resulting in sleet and freezing rain to mix in. In terms of accumulations, snowfall amounts (which include sleet) averaged 7 to 10. If you separate sleet, a general 3 to 5 inches were reported across the district. Freezing rain amounts of a trace to locally a tenth of an inch were observed as well. To capture the true magnitude of this event, the actual melted liquid with this storm was near 2 inches.

A rather anomalous Arctic Outbreak settled in ahead of the January 25th Winter Storm with reinforcing shots through the last week of January. The remarkable aspect of this outbreak was the duration, especially for the Mid-Atlantic. The coldest nights (January 27th, 30th, and 31st) featured Extreme Cold Warnings with air temperatures in the single digits and wind chills as low as -10F. Other nights, Cold Weather Advisories resulted in wind chills near 0F. The coldest wind chills were overnight.

A powerful early season cold front spawned multiple rounds of severe thunderstorms. The first round occurred from late morning through mid afternoon, and focused mainly across northern Virginia into north-central Maryland producing scattered wind damage and a brief tornado. As the front itself crossed the region during the evening, a line of low-topped convection aided in the mixing down of an intense low-level jet, resulting in widespread 60 to 70 mph wind gusts near and east of the Blue Ridge and Catoctin Mountains.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A large tree blew down along Canal Road Northwest.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Another shot of Arctic Air spilled in February 7th through February 9th. Minimum wind chills around 0 to as low as -10F were observed. The coldest wind chills were overnight.

A rather anomalous Arctic Outbreak continued into the first couple days of February. The remarkable aspect of this outbreak was the duration, as it extends well back into January. Minimum wind chills of -10 to -20F were observed. The coldest wind chills were overnight.

A strong Nor'Easter moved northward along the Eastern Seaboard February 22nd into the 23rd. Temperatures were marginal to start resulting in primarily rain during the daylight hours of February 22nd. Near sunset, rain changed to snow which continued into the overnight. Total snow accumulations of 1 to 4 inches were observed in the District of Columbia.
A strong upper trough and Arctic high pressure over the Mid-Atlantic combined to produce a period of high winds.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: The ASOS at Washington Reagan National Airport, KDCA, measured a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
